segments.text: 30 minutes of snoozing cost only about 6 minutes of sleep.
That's what one lab study measured in 31 regular snoozers.
We're told snoozing wrecks your morning. Here, it didn't.
Compared with waking abruptly, the snoozers did as well or better on thinking tests right after getting up.
So skip the guilt and make a plan. Decide your snooze window the night before, then stand up when the last alarm rings.
Try it today: decide your snooze window before bed.
